title: Pseudo-coherent reconstruction over inverse limits of nilpotent ring quotients
statement: Let $(A_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse system of commutative rings with surjective transition maps and nilpotent kernels (a kernel $J$ is nilpotent when $J^r=0$ for some $r\geq1$), and put $A=\varprojlim_n A_n$, the ring of compatible tuples with componentwise operations. Let $E_n\in D(A_n)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] have maps $t_n:E_{n+1}\to E_n$ in $D(A_{n+1})$ inducing isomorphisms $E_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\simeq E_n$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. If $E_1$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], then $E=R\varprojlim_n E_n$, formed after restriction to $A$ [def-weil-derived-limit], is pseudo-coherent and the projection-induced maps $E\otimes_A^L A_n\to E_n$ are isomorphisms. More precisely, there are bounded-above complexes $P_n^\bullet$ of finite free $A_n$-modules, with a common upper cutoff, representing the $E_n$, and surjective chain transitions representing $t_n$ whose reduction maps $P_{n+1}^\bullet\otimes_{A_{n+1}}A_n\to P_n^\bullet$ are chain isomorphisms. Their termwise limit $P^\bullet=\varprojlim_nP_n^\bullet$ is bounded above finite free over $A$, represents $E$ respecting its projections, and $P^\bullet\otimes_A A_n\to P_n^\bullet$ is a chain isomorphism for every $n$. These chain isomorphisms represent the projection-induced derived comparison maps.

source.place: Tag 0CQF, lemma-Rlim-pseudo-coherent-gives-pseudo-coherent, statement and proof (compatible finite-free models and projection-induced reductions)

proof.text: Induct on $n$ to show that every $E_n$ is pseudo-coherent. The base $n=1$ is assumed. At the induction step apply nilpotent invariance to $A_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_n$ and $E_{n+1}$: its derived reduction is isomorphic to $E_n$ by the specified transition. Thus the pseudo-coherence of $E_n$ implies that of $E_{n+1}$. Choose a bounded-above finite-free representative $P_1^\bullet$ of $E_1$, an isomorphism $\beta_1:Q(P_1^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}E_1$, and an integer $b$ above which it is zero.

Suppose $P_n$, $\beta_n$, and the transitions through level $n$ have been chosen, with $P_n^i=0$ for $i>b$. Set $I=\ker(A_{n+1}\to A_n)$. If $I^N=0$, each $1+x$ with $x\in I$ has inverse $\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(-x)^j$. Apply marked free-complex lifting to $R=A_{n+1}$, $R/I=A_n$, $K=E_{n+1}$, $F=P_n$, and the specified isomorphism $\alpha=\beta_n^{-1}\circ\overline t_n:E_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(P_n)$, where $\overline t_n$ is induced by $t_n$. This gives $P_{n+1}$ zero above the same $b$, $\beta_{n+1}$, and $\theta_n:P_{n+1}\otimes_{A_{n+1}}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}P_n$, with $Q(\theta_n)=\beta_n^{-1}\overline t_n(\beta_{n+1}\otimes^L A_n)$. Define $u_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$ as the quotient map followed by $\theta_n$. It is a chain map, degreewise surjective, and the marking equation says that it represents the given transition $t_n$ under the $\beta$'s. Repeating this induction constructs the entire strictly compatible complex tower.

source.place: Tag 0CQF, induction using Tag 0BCB (lemma-lift-complex-stably-frees); prescribed marking as in the existing marked lifting statement

proof.text: Construct compatible finite bases separately in each degree $i$. Choose a basis of $P_1^i$ of size $r_i$. Given the basis at level $n$, lift its vectors through the surjection $u_n^i$ to $P_{n+1}^i$. They form a basis: put $R=A_{n+1}$ and let $f:R^{r_i}\to P_{n+1}^i$ send the standard vectors to these lifts. Its reduction modulo $I$ is an isomorphism. Since $P_{n+1}^i$ is finite free, lift the matrix of the inverse reduced map to an $R$-linear $g:P_{n+1}^i\to R^{r_i}$. Both $gf-1$ and $fg-1$ have matrices in $I$; their $N$th powers vanish, so geometric sums invert $gf$ and $fg$. Consequently $f$ has a left inverse $(gf)^{-1}g$ and a right inverse $g(fg)^{-1}$; these coincide, and $f$ is an isomorphism. This also covers $r_i=0$. The bases so constructed make $u_n^i$ the coordinatewise ring reduction $A_{n+1}^{r_i}\to A_n^{r_i}$.

source.place: Tag 0CQF, sentence asserting the limit terms are finite free; explicit compatible-basis argument

proof.text: Let $P^i=\varprojlim_n P_n^i$, with differential $(x_n)\mapsto(d_nx_n)$; compatibility follows from $u_nd_{n+1}=d_nu_n$, and $d^2=0$ holds coordinatewise. In the compatible bases of step 3, a compatible vector tuple is exactly $r_i$ compatible scalar tuples, so $P^i\cong(\varprojlim_n A_n)^{r_i}=A^{r_i}$. All $P^i$ vanish for $i>b$. Projection is coordinatewise $A^{r_i}\to A_n^{r_i}$. Therefore $P^i\otimes_A A_n\to P_n^i$, $(x_m)_m\otimes a\mapsto ax_n$, is an isomorphism. Its inverse in these bases sends the $j$th standard vector to the compatible $j$th basis tuple tensor $1$. The projections commute with differentials, so these degreewise maps assemble into chain isomorphisms $P^\bullet\otimes_A A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}P_n^\bullet$.

source.place: Tag 0CQF, final three sentences; explicit coordinates and projection compatibility

proof.text: Restrict all $P_n$ to $A$. The maps $u_n$ are degreewise surjective, so the surjective module-complex tower lemma identifies $Q(P)$, with its literal projections, as a derived limit of $(Q(P_n),Q(u_n))$ in $D(A)$. The compatible isomorphisms $\beta_n$ identify this system with $(E_n,t_n)$; the induced isomorphism of products is obtained componentwise, with inverse the product of the $\beta_n^{-1}$. It conjugates $1-s$ to $1-s$ because $\beta_nQ(u_n)=t_n\beta_{n+1}$. Write $B_P=\prod_nQ(P_n)$, $B_E=\prod_nE_n$, $v=\prod_n\beta_n:B_P\xrightarrow{\sim}B_E$, and let $j:Q(P)\to B_P$ and $\delta_P:B_P\to Q(P)[1]$ be the arrows of its Roos triangle. The triangle $Q(P)\xrightarrow{vj}B_E\xrightarrow{1-s}B_E\xrightarrow{\delta_Pv^{-1}}Q(P)[1]$ is isomorphic to that triangle by $(1,v,v)$: the first square is $vj=vj$, the second is $v(1-s)=(1-s)v$, and the last is $(\delta_Pv^{-1})v=\delta_P$. Thus TR1 makes it distinguished, with projections $\beta_nQ(P\to P_n)$. Compare with the chosen Roos triangle defining $E$: rotate both triangles so $1-s$ is their first arrow, use TR3 with identities on the two product objects, and rotate back. The triangle isomorphism lemma makes the resulting map $Q(P)\to E$ an isomorphism. The first square says it respects every projection. No canonical choice of this isomorphism is asserted.

proof.text: A finite free module is flat: its tensor functor is a finite direct sum of the identity functor, hence preserves exact sequences componentwise. Thus the bounded-above complexes $P$ over $A$ and $P_n$ over $A_n$ are K-flat by the bounded-flat K-flat criterion. On the category with one object and only its identity morphism, a presheaf is its value at that object and the identity-cover sheaf condition imposes no restriction. Ring sheaves, module sheaves, their complexes and tensor products are therefore ordinary rings, modules, complexes and tensor products. Derived change of rings on this site computes $Q(P)\otimes_A^L A_n$ by the ordinary tensor complex $P\otimes_A A_n$. Under the projection-respecting isomorphism in step 5, the projection-induced comparison is represented by the chain map $P\otimes_A A_n\to P_n$, $x\otimes a\mapsto a\,\mathrm{pr}_n(x)$, followed by $\beta_n$. To justify that this is the specified derived map, use the scalar-extension Hom bijection degreewise: $f:P\to P_n$ corresponds to $\widetilde f:P\otimes_A A_n\to P_n$, $\widetilde f(x\otimes a)=af(x)$. The chain-map equations correspond under this bijection by evaluating on $x\otimes1$, and a homotopy $h$ corresponds to $\widetilde h(x\otimes a)=ah(x)$, since $d\widetilde h+\widetilde h d$ is the transpose of $dh+hd$. Hence it is a bijection on homotopy classes. Every finite free module is projective: lift a map through a surjection by choosing a preimage for each basis vector. Both $P$ over $A$ and $P\otimes_A A_n$ over $A_n$ are bounded above projective. The derived-map-representative lemma identifies both homotopy Hom sets with their derived Hom sets. We therefore obtain a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_n)}(Q(P\otimes_A A_n),Q(P_n))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(Q(P),Q(P_n))$, computed by composition with $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. In particular the transpose of the projection is exactly the displayed chain map. Composing with the markings and the projection-respecting isomorphism of step 5 gives precisely the projection-induced derived comparison. This calculation also justifies the transition-map representation from the marking equation in step 2, with $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ in place of $A\to A_n$. Step 4 proves this chain map is an isomorphism, so the derived comparison is an isomorphism. Finally $P$ is bounded above finite free by step 4 and represents $E$ by step 5, which proves pseudo-coherence by its definition and all the more precise clauses.
